text: 私を消しても
translation: Even if you destroy me...

vocabulary.meaning: to erase, to destroy, to extinguish

grammar: 〜ても is a concessive conditional: 'even if you do X, (something still holds).' The sentence trails off, implying what follows (スピラの悲しみは消えはしない).

text: スピラの悲しみは消えはしない
translation: Spira's sorrow will never disappear.
grammar: 消えはしない uses the は particle inserted before しない to create emphatic negation — stronger than just 消えない. It carries a sense of 'will absolutely not disappear.' This is Yu Yevon / Sin speaking.

text: シンゴと消してやるよ
translation: I'll wipe it out along with Sin!

vocabulary.meaning: to erase, to destroy, to wipe out
to do (something) for someone (often with a defiant or emphatic nuance)

grammar: シンごと is written as シンゴと in the subtitle (likely a transcription quirk); it means 'together with Sin / Sin and all.' 〜てやる adds a determined, almost aggressive nuance: 'I'll do it (for you / just watch me).'

text: おすいぞ アーロン
translation: You're impressive, Auron.

vocabulary.meaning: impressive, not bad (archaic/dialectal form of 見事/なかなか; here Jecht's rough speech)

grammar: おすいぞ is Jecht's rough, masculine speech. The final ぞ asserts the statement emphatically. This is Jecht acknowledging Auron inside Sin.

text: つつま
translation: (Indistinct / partial utterance — likely 「包まれた」or similar, part of a cut line)

text: まだ、あんたのほうがデカい
translation: You're still bigger than me.
grammar: AのほうがB is the standard comparative: 'A is more [adjective] than B.' Here the B (俺/me) is omitted — Tidus is comparing himself to Jecht.

text: なんつっても俺はシンだからな
translation: Well, I am Sin after all.

vocabulary.meaning: after all, no matter what you say (colloquial contraction of なんといっても)
because ~, after all ~ (casual sentence ending seeking acknowledgment)

grammar: なんつっても is a colloquial contraction of なんといっても ('no matter what anyone says / after all'). The な at the end is a masculine sentence-final particle seeking light agreement.

text: 笑えないっつうの
translation: That's not funny, you know.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to laugh, to find funny
I'm telling you ~, you know ~ (colloquial emphatic)

grammar: 笑えない is the negative potential form of 笑う: 'cannot laugh / not funny.' っつうの (contraction of っていうの) is a colloquial emphatic ending expressing mild exasperation.

text: じゃあ、まあなんだ / その…
translation: Well then, I mean... / Um...
grammar: A series of filler expressions showing Jecht struggling to say something meaningful to Tidus. その… trails off — a very natural way to show hesitation in Japanese.

text: 蹴りつけっか?
translation: Want me to give you a kick?

vocabulary.meaning: to kick hard, to give a kick to
shall I ~?, want me to ~? (rough colloquial question)

grammar: 蹴りつけっか is a rough contraction of 蹴りつけるか — Jecht offering in his own awkward way to connect with Tidus through their blitzball tradition (the kick that started Tidus's story).

text: 親父…
translation: Dad...

text: 馬鹿
translation: Idiot.

vocabulary.meaning: idiot, fool; also used as a term of rough affection

grammar: Said with affection rather than contempt — Jecht's way of expressing emotion without being sentimental.

text: それでいいさ
translation: That's fine. That's enough.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle: light assertion, 'you know,' 'that's just how it is'

text: どうすりゃいいかわかってんな
translation: You know what to do, right?

vocabulary.meaning: what to do, how to handle
if (one) does ~ (colloquial contraction of すれば)
you do ~, don't you (colloquial contraction with confirming な)

grammar: どうすりゃいいかわかってんな is a colloquial chain: どうすれば + いいか (what's good) + わかっているな (you understand, right?). Jecht is confirming Tidus knows what must be done.

text: もう歌もあんまし 聞こえねえんだ
translation: I can barely hear the song anymore.

vocabulary.meaning: not very much, barely (colloquial form of あまり)
to be audible, to be heard

grammar: 聞こえねえんだ: 聞こえない (can't hear) → rough colloquial 聞こえねえ + んだ (explanatory). The 'song' refers to Yuna's sending prayer/hymn that has kept Jecht's consciousness alive inside Sin.

text: もうちょっとで 俺は 心の底からシンになっちまう
translation: A little longer and I'll become Sin from the bottom of my heart.

vocabulary.meaning: a little more, a bit longer
the depths of one's heart, from the bottom of one's heart
to end up doing ~, to completely do ~ (colloquial contraction of てしまう)

grammar: もうちょっとで means 'just a bit more and...' — implying an imminent undesirable outcome. 〜ちまう (from てしまう) expresses completion with a sense of regret or inevitability. Jecht explains his consciousness is almost fully subsumed by Sin.

text: 間に合って助かったぜ
translation: Good thing you made it in time.

vocabulary.meaning: to be in time, to make it on time
to be saved, to be a relief, to be helpful

grammar: 助かったぜ: 助かる normally means 'to be rescued' but also idiomatically means 'what a relief / I'm grateful.' Jecht is expressing relief that Tidus arrived before he was completely consumed.

text: でよ、始まっちまったら、俺は壊れちまう。
translation: Once it starts, I'll be destroyed.

vocabulary.meaning: and, so (rough colloquial connective; contraction of それでよ or でも)

grammar: 始まっちまったら: the conditional 〜たら attached to the 〜ちまう form — 'once it ends up starting.' でよ is a rough masculine connective.

text: 手加減とか、できねえからよ。
translation: I won't be able to hold back or anything like that.

vocabulary.meaning: holding back, going easy on someone, moderation of force

grammar: Jecht warns that once the battle begins, he will be fully Sin with no restraint. 手加減できない means 'cannot hold back.' とか softens the list. からよ gives a causal explanation in a rough masculine register.

text: すまねえな。 / もういいって。
translation: Sorry about that. / That's enough of that.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm sorry, forgive me (rough form of 申し訳ない)
that's enough, it's fine, stop it
I said ~, you know ~ (colloquial emphatic quotative)

grammar: すまねえ is Jecht's rough apology. Tidus's もういいって uses the quotative って as an emphatic 'I'm telling you, that's enough.' A small but emotionally loaded exchange.

text: うだうだ言ってないでさ。
translation: Stop going on and on about it.

vocabulary.meaning: going on and on, hemming and hawing, whining repetitively

grammar: うだうだ is a mimetic word (擬態語) meaning to go on and on pointlessly. 言ってないで = 'without saying / instead of saying.' Tidus is telling Jecht to stop apologizing.

text: だな。
translation: Yeah, you're right.
grammar: A minimal acknowledgment — Jecht agreeing with Tidus's point.

text: 자, 이처에 가볼까?
translation: (Korean subtitle — not Japanese dialogue. Likely: 'Well then, shall we go?')

text: 泣くぞ / すぐ泣くぞ
translation: I'm going to cry. / I'm going to cry right away.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle: masculine assertion or warning

grammar: 泣くぞ here functions as a warning or self-prediction: 'I'm going to cry (so watch out).' The repeated lines build comic/emotional tension as Wakka and others struggle to hold back tears.

text: 絶対泣くぞ / ほら泣くぞ
translation: I'm definitely going to cry. / See, I'm crying!
grammar: ほら泣くぞ uses ほら as a 'see, I told you so' exclamation — the speaker is now actually crying and pointing it out.

text: 大嫌いだ
translation: I hate you. (Said with love — the iconic farewell to Tidus.)

vocabulary.meaning: to really hate, to strongly dislike

grammar: 大 intensifies 嫌い ('dislike') to 'really hate.' In context this is Yuna's paradoxical goodbye — saying 'I hate you' to express overwhelming love and grief. One of the most emotionally resonant lines in the game.

text: まだ早いぜ
translation: Not yet — it's too soon.

text: 全部
translation: Everything —

text: 終わらせてからだよな
translation: ...after we finish everything. Right?

vocabulary.meaning: to finish, to bring to an end (causative of 終わる)

grammar: 終わらせてから: causative form 終わらせる + てから (after). Tidus tells himself/the group to hold off grief until after the mission is done. だよな seeks light confirmation.

text: わかってるじゃねえか / さすがチェクト様のガキだ
translation: You do understand! / Expected nothing less from Jecht's kid.

vocabulary.meaning: aren't you!, you are! (rough surprised/pleased exclamation)
as expected of, just like ~ (expressing admiration)

grammar: じゃねえか (rough form of じゃないか) expresses surprised approval. さすが～様 uses an honorific on Jecht (チェクト様) with rough ガキ — a typical Jecht-style mix of reverence and roughness.

text: 初めて思った
translation: I thought that for the first time.
grammar: The subject (俺) is omitted. Tidus is saying he thought, for the first time, that he's glad to be Jecht's son — which he expresses in the next two lines.

text: あんたの息子で
translation: That I am your son —
grammar: で here is the te-form of だ, connecting to the following clause よかった: 'being your son was/is good.'

text: よかった / ケッ
translation: I'm glad. / Hmph.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm glad, that was good (past tense of いい)

grammar: あんたの息子でよかった: 'it was good being your son / I'm glad I'm your son.' One of the most emotionally loaded short lines in the game. Jecht's ケッ is his way of deflecting the emotion.

text: チェクトさん / あの…
translation: Jecht — / Um...
grammar: Yuna begins to address Jecht (チェクト is how his name is rendered in Japanese; she uses the polite さん). あの… is a common hesitation opener.

text: ダメだ / ユーナちゃん
translation: No good. / Yuna.
grammar: Jecht cuts Yuna off — ダメだ meaning 'there's no time / don't start.' He calls her ユーナちゃん with the affectionate suffix, showing his fondness for her.

text: 時間がねえ
translation: There's no time.

vocabulary.meaning: there isn't (rough colloquial negation of ある)

text: 邪魔するじゃねえ! / ユーナちゃん / わかってんな
translation: Don't interfere! / Yuna. / You understand, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to interfere, to get in the way
don't ~ (rough prohibition; contraction of じゃないか used as command)

grammar: 邪魔するじゃねえ is a rough prohibition: 'don't interfere!' Jecht is addressing both the aeons and Yuna — they must not prevent the final battle. わかってんな seeks confirmation.

text: 召喚獣を / 僕たちを
translation: The aeons — / us —

vocabulary.meaning: summoned beast, aeon (the summoned creatures in FFX)

grammar: These are object markers (を) with no verb yet — the sentence continues in clip_038. Yuna/Tidus completing each other's thought: 'Call the aeons / call us.'

text: 呼ぶんだぞ / 呼ぶんだよ
translation: Call them, okay! / Call us, okay!

vocabulary.meaning: make sure to ~, you hear me! (emphatic instruction with masculine ぞ)
make sure to ~, okay! (emphatic instruction, slightly softer)

grammar: Jecht says 召喚獣を呼ぶんだぞ (call your aeons!); Tidus echoes with 僕たちを呼ぶんだよ (call us!). Both are strong exhortations using んだ for emphasis.

text: ユーラ!
translation: Yuna!
grammar: ユーラ appears to be a transcription variant of ユウナ (Yuna), likely a mishearing or subtitle error. In context Tidus is calling out to Yuna during the battle.

text: みんな!
translation: Everyone!

text: 一緒に戦えるのは、これが最後だ!
translation: This is the last time we'll fight together!

vocabulary.meaning: the fact that one can ~ (nominalizing potential form)

grammar: 一緒に戦える is the potential form of 戦う: 'can fight together.' Nominalized with のは and followed by これが最後だ: 'this [time] is the last.' Tidus rallying the party before the final battle.

text: よろしく!
translation: Let's do this! / I'm counting on you all!

vocabulary.meaning: please (take care of things), I'm counting on you, let's go (versatile social phrase)

grammar: よろしく as a standalone exclamation before a fight means something like 'I'm in your hands' or 'let's do this together.'

text: なんつったらいいかな
translation: I don't know how to put this...

vocabulary.meaning: what would be good / how should I...

grammar: なんつったら is a colloquial contraction of なんといったら. The whole phrase なんつったらいいかな means 'what should I say, I wonder' — Tidus searching for words before his farewell announcement.

text: エボンジュを倒したら
translation: When we defeat Yu Yevon —
grammar: 〜たら here is a temporal conditional: 'when we defeat Yu Yevon' (not 'if'). The sentence continues in the next clip.

text: 俺、消えっから
translation: I'm going to disappear.

vocabulary.meaning: to disappear, to vanish, to fade away
because ~, so ~ (rough colloquial form of から)

grammar: 消えっから is a rough contraction of 消えるから: 'I'm going to disappear, so...' Tidus tells his companions the truth about his fate for the first time.

text: あんた、何言ってんのよ
translation: What are you talking about?
grammar: 何言ってんのよ: 何 + 言っている (contracted to 言ってん) + のよ. The feminine のよ and tone indicate shock/disbelief — likely Rikku responding to Tidus's revelation.

text: さよならってこと! / そんな...
translation: It means goodbye! / No, that can't be...

vocabulary.meaning: it means that ~, in other words ~
such a thing, that kind of thing (often trailing off in disbelief)

grammar: 〜ってこと is a colloquial form of 〜ということ: 'it means/amounts to saying goodbye.' そんな… trailing off expresses stunned disbelief — a party member refusing to accept it.

text: 勝手で悪いけどさ、これが俺の物語だ!
translation: Sorry for being selfish about it, but this is my story!

vocabulary.meaning: selfishness, doing as one pleases, acting unilaterally
sorry for being ~, bad that it's ~ (apologetic construction)
but, though (casual connective with さ softening)

grammar: 勝手で悪いけど is an apologetic opening: 'I know it's selfish of me, but.' これが俺の物語だ is the definitive declaration — echoing the game's opening narration. A full-circle moment.

text: Субтитры создавал DimaTorzok
translation: (Russian subtitle watermark: 'Subtitles created by DimaTorzok' — not game dialogue)

text: 続けろ / でも…
translation: Keep going. / But...
grammar: 続けろ is the plain imperative of 続ける — a command to go on. でも… trails off in protest/hesitation. Context: after Yu Yevon is defeated, Tidus tells Yuna to continue the sending as he begins to fade.

text: これでいいぞ
translation: This is how it should be.

vocabulary.meaning: this is fine, this is how it should be

text: 10年、待たせたからな
translation: I made you wait 10 years, after all.

vocabulary.meaning: to make someone wait (causative of 待つ)

grammar: 待たせた is the causative past of 待つ: 'I made (you) wait.' Auron speaks to Jecht here — they have been waiting 10 years for this moment, and now Auron can finally be sent.

text: もう、お前たちの時代だ
translation: Now it's your era — your time.
grammar: Auron's final words before being sent — passing the torch to the younger generation. もう marks that the transition has arrived.

text: 俺…帰らなくちゃ!
translation: I... have to go back!
grammar: 帰らなくちゃ is a colloquial contraction of 帰らなくてはいけない: 'I have to go back.' Tidus is beginning to fade and runs toward the airship bow — the iconic farewell scene begins.

text: ザナルカウント案内できなくて、ごめんな!
translation: Sorry I couldn't show you Zanarkand!

vocabulary.meaning: not being able to ~ (te-form of できない, leading to apology)

grammar: 〜できなくて + ごめん is a natural pattern for apologizing for inability: 'sorry that I couldn't do X.' Tidus is apologizing to Wakka (or the group) for not fulfilling his promise to take them to Zanarkand. ザナルカウントは likely a subtitle variant of ザナルカンド.

text: じゃあな! / えっ?
translation: See ya! / Huh?
grammar: じゃあな is a classic casual masculine goodbye — Tidus bidding farewell as he runs past each party member.

text: また会えるんだよね? / ねえ?
translation: We'll meet again, right? / Right?

vocabulary.meaning: we can ~, right? (potential + んだ + よね seeking confirmation)

grammar: また会えるんだよね: potential form 会える + んだ (explanatory) + よね (seeking confirmation). The repeated ねえ? expresses desperate hope. This is Rikku calling after Tidus.

text: ユーノ! / 快
translation: Yuna! / (affirmative grunt)
grammar: ユーノ appears to be a subtitle transcription variant of ユウナ. 快 (かい/こころよい) as a standalone character here may be a subtitle artifact or a short affirmation sound.

text: ありがとう
translation: Thank you.
grammar: Said by Tidus to Yuna (or vice versa) at the moment of farewell. One of the simplest but most emotionally devastating lines of the ending.

text: 言うな サラサラ
translation: (Don't say anything — just let it flow.) / [Possible subtitle artifact]

vocabulary.meaning: flowing smoothly; also: not at all (in negative: さらさらない)

grammar: 言うな is a direct negative imperative: 'don't say it.' サラサラ (or さらさら) may be part of song lyrics or a subtitle artifact. Context is Yuna's address to Spira.

text: 多くの数え切れない犠牲がありました
translation: There were many, countless sacrifices.

vocabulary.meaning: many, much (adverbial form of 多い)
countless, too many to count (lit. cannot finish counting)
there were (polite past of ある)

grammar: 数え切れない is a compound potential negative: 数える (to count) + 切れない (cannot finish). Yuna's public address uses polite ます/ました forms throughout, marking formal speech.

text: 何をなくしたのかわからないくらいたくさん なくしました
translation: We lost so much that we don't even know what we lost.

vocabulary.meaning: to the extent of ~, so much that ~

grammar: 何をなくしたのかわからないくらい is a complex nominalized structure: 'to the extent that we don't know what we lost.' The repetition of なくす (lost) frames the enormity of the sacrifices.

text: その代わり もう / シンはいません
translation: But in exchange — Sin is gone now.

vocabulary.meaning: in exchange, but in return, however
to exist, to be (for animate beings)
is not here, does not exist (polite negative of いる)

grammar: その代わり sets up a contrast: 'we lost so much, but in return — Sin no longer exists.' もう + negative (いません) = 'no longer.'

text: もしません
translation: Nor will it ever again.

vocabulary.meaning: will not do ~ either (emphatic negation, adding completeness)

grammar: もしません adds to シンはいません — 'Sin is not here and will not [return/act] either.' The も intensifies the negation, making it absolute.

text: これから
translation: From now on —

text: これからは 私たちの時代
translation: From now on, it is our era.

vocabulary.meaning: from now on (は emphasizes the temporal shift)

grammar: The は in これからは is a topic marker highlighting the temporal contrast with the past age of Sin. Echoes Auron's earlier もうお前たちの時代だ.

text: だよね
translation: Right?
grammar: The shift from formal address to the informal だよね is touching — Yuna momentarily drops the public speaker register and speaks personally to the crowd.

text: いっぱいあるけど 時間もいっぱいあるから
translation: There's a lot [to deal with], but we also have a lot of time.
grammar: The subject of the first いっぱいある is implied from context — problems/things to do. The も in 時間もいっぱい adds 'time too / time also.' から here gives a soft causal/reassuring tone.

text: だから 大丈夫だよね
translation: So it'll be alright, right?
grammar: Yuna's reassurance is itself a question — she is not certain but choosing to believe it will be okay. The よね pulls the listener in to agree with her hope.

text: 力を合わせて 一緒に歩けるよね
translation: We can combine our strength and walk forward together, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to combine strength, to join forces

grammar: 力を合わせて is the te-form used as 'by combining our strength.' 歩ける is the potential of 歩く. よね again pulls for collective agreement.

text: 一つだけお願いがあります
translation: There is just one thing I ask of you.
grammar: A formal, polite request opening. Yuna returns to formal register (あります) for this important petition to the people of Spira.

text: いなくなってしまった人たちのこと
translation: The people who are no longer with us —

vocabulary.meaning: to no longer be here, to disappear (of animate beings)

grammar: いなくなってしまった人たち: those who have gone (including Tidus, Auron, Jecht, and all who died). のこと sets up the next clause's topic — 'about those people.'

text: 時々でいいから
translation: Just every now and then —

vocabulary.meaning: it's fine just with ~, just ~ is enough
because, so (here: soft 'just because it's enough' tone)

grammar: 時々でいいから: 'it's fine just every now and then / just sometimes is enough.' A gentle, humble request — Yuna is not asking for constant remembrance, just occasional thought.

text: 思い出してください
translation: Please remember them.
grammar: The culmination of Yuna's plea: 思い出してください — 'please remember (them).' This completes the sentence started at clip_072. A formal, heartfelt petition.

text: 風が寄せた言葉に
translation: In the words carried on the wind,

vocabulary.meaning: to bring near, to carry (toward), to draw close

grammar: Song lyrics begin here (「素敵だね」). 風が寄せた言葉に: に marks 'in / upon the words that the wind carried.' 寄せた is the past attributive form modifying 言葉.

text: 泳いだ心
translation: A heart that swam (was swept away).

vocabulary.meaning: to swim; figuratively: to be swept away, to drift

grammar: 泳いだ心: past attributive — 'a heart that swam/drifted.' 風が寄せた言葉に泳いだ心: 'a heart that swam in the words carried by the wind.' Lyrical, imagistic.

text: 雲が運ぶ明日に 弾んだ声
translation: A voice that leapt with joy, toward a tomorrow that clouds carry.

vocabulary.meaning: to bounce, to be lively, to be buoyant with excitement

grammar: 雲が運ぶ明日に: 'toward a tomorrow that the clouds carry.' 弾んだ声: 'a voice that bounced/was buoyant.' Parallel structure to the previous line — natural image in/toward X + emotional response Y.

text: 月が揺れる鏡に 震えた心
translation: A heart that trembled, in the mirror where the moon sways.

vocabulary.meaning: to sway, to rock, to waver
to tremble, to shake, to quiver

grammar: 月が揺れる鏡: 'a mirror in which the moon sways' — a watery surface reflecting moonlight. に marks the location in which the trembling occurred. Another parallel imagistic structure.

text: 星が流れこぼれた やわらかい涙
translation: Soft tears that flowed and spilled like falling stars.
grammar: 星が流れこぼれた is a compound verbal phrase: 流れる + こぼれる combined as one action — 'streamed and spilled over.' やわらかい涙 is the noun phrase it modifies.

text: 素敵だね 二人手を取り歩けたなら
translation: How wonderful it would be, if the two of us could hold hands and walk together.

vocabulary.meaning: two people, the two of us
to take someone's hand, to hold hands

grammar: 歩けたなら: potential past 歩けた + なら = 'if only we could walk.' The たなら structure often implies a wish or hypothetical ('if that were to happen / if only'). This is the chorus of 素敵だね, the FFX ending theme.

text: 行きたいよ 君の街家 上の中
translation: I want to go — to your town, inside your heart. (Subtitle transcription may be imprecise)
grammar: 行きたいよ is a heartfelt 'I want to go' with よ adding personal assertion. The rest of the lyric (君の街家 上の中) may be a subtitle transcription imprecision for 「君の街へ 夢の中」('to your town, inside a dream') — a common lyric in the song.

text: その胸 からだあつけ
translation: To your chest — pressed close to your body. (Likely: 「その胸 体あずけ」— entrusting my body to your chest)

vocabulary.meaning: to entrust, to leave in someone's care

grammar: Likely 体あずけ = 体を預け: 'entrusting my body (to you)' — a lyric about leaning into an embrace. The subtitle appears to have a transcription imprecision.

text: 夜に庭切れ 夢見る
translation: Dreaming, lost in the night. (Likely: 「夜に紛れ 夢見る」— blending into the night, dreaming)

vocabulary.meaning: to be lost in, to blend into, to become indistinct within

grammar: 夜に紛れ: 'blending into the night / lost in the night' (te-form of 紛れる). 夢見る: to dream. A lyric about disappearing into night and dreaming.

text: 手は止まり言葉は やさしい幻
translation: Hands stop moving, and words become a gentle illusion.
grammar: 手は止まり: は marks topic/contrast, まり is the te-form of 止まる. 言葉はやさしい幻: 'words are a gentle illusion.' The contrastive は (手は / 言葉は) creates parallel structure.

text: 雲は破れ 明日は遠くも越え
translation: Clouds break apart, and tomorrow crosses even far distances.

vocabulary.meaning: to tear, to break, to be torn apart
to cross over, to surpass, to go beyond

grammar: 雲は破れ: te-form (破れ) creating sequence. 明日は遠くも越え: 'tomorrow crosses even far distances' — も adds 'even.' The も emphasizes that even great distances are overcome.

text: 月がにじむ鏡を 流れた心
translation: A heart that flowed through a mirror where the moon blurs.

vocabulary.meaning: to blur, to bleed (of ink/color), to be hazy

grammar: 月がにじむ鏡: 'a mirror in which the moon blurs' — moonlight on a rippling water surface. を marks the object/path of 流れた: 'flowed through/across.' A variation of the earlier 揺れる/震えた verse.

text: 星が揺れてこぼれた 隠せない涙
translation: Tears that cannot be hidden, as stars wavered and spilled over.
grammar: 星が揺れてこぼれた: te-form sequence — 'the stars wavered and spilled over.' 隠せない涙: 'tears that cannot be hidden' (negative potential as attributive). A variation of やわらかい涙 from the first verse.

text: 素敵だね 二人手を取りあげたなら
translation: How wonderful it would be, if the two of us could raise our joined hands.

vocabulary.meaning: two people, the two of us
to raise up; to do (for someone's benefit)

grammar: 取りあげた is a compound: 取る + 上げる = 'to take up / raise (hands together).' A variation of the first chorus line (歩けたなら → 取りあげたなら).

text: 生きたいよ 君の街へ 生んでこまる
translation: I want to live — toward your town... (subtitle transcription may be imprecise)
grammar: 生きたいよ: 'I want to live' — a shift from 行きたいよ (want to go) in the first verse, deepening the emotional register. 生んでこまる may be a subtitle transcription error.

text: その顔 そっと触れて 朝に溶ける夢見る
translation: Gently touching that face, dreaming of a dream that melts into the morning.
grammar: そっと触れて: te-form creating sequence — 'touching gently, and...' 朝に溶ける夢: 'a dream that melts into the morning' (溶ける as attributive modifying 夢). 夢見る: dreaming of that dream.

text: 好きだね 二人手を取り歩けたなら
translation: I love you — how wonderful if the two of us could hold hands and walk together.
grammar: 好きだね shifts from 素敵だね (wonderful) to the direct 'I love you / I like you.' A more personal, intimate declaration. The chorus lyric returns with this emotional deepening.

text: 生きたいよ 君の街家 腕を巻く
translation: I want to live — in your town, arms wrapped around you.
grammar: 腕を巻く: 'wrapping arms (around you)' — an embrace. Builds on the earlier verse's imagery of physical closeness (体あずけ → 腕を巻く).

text: その胸 体あつけ
translation: To your chest, entrusting my body. (Likely: 「その胸 体あずけ」)
grammar: Repeat of clip_082 lyric — its place in the final chorus emphasizes the longing for closeness and rest.

text: 夜に紛れ 夢に舞う
translation: Lost in the night, dancing in a dream.

vocabulary.meaning: to be lost in, to blend into
to dance, to flutter, to soar

grammar: 夜に紛れ: te-form of 紛れる — 'blending into the night.' 夢に舞う: 'dancing in a dream.' に marks location/medium for both actions. A beautiful final lyric closing the ending — Tidus (as a dream) dissolves into the night and dances in the dream world.
